answer: Part IV, Running the School, covers teacher planning and grading, assessment and data, operations and finance, and people and leadership. These chapters speak most directly to principals, district leaders, and board members.

children.name: Teacher Planning, Grading, and Feedback
children.blurb: Fifteen teachers in five primary schools in England used AI to help plan lessons for two school terms. Their self reported weekly planning time fell by 52.5 percent, from about 10 hours to under 5 (Carson et al., 2026).

children.name: Assessment, Data, and the Early Warning System
children.blurb: Researchers who build systems to predict student failure found something troubling when they looked closely. A single accuracy number made predictions look more reliable than they were.

children.name: Operations, Facilities, Transportation, and Finance
children.blurb: Boston Public Schools once faced a transportation problem that cost more than $100 million a year. Researchers built an optimization system that redesigned the bus routes, saving about $5 million a year and removing 50 buses while keeping service quality (Bertsimas et al., 2019).

children.name: People, Leadership, and Culture
children.blurb: Researchers interviewed leaders in six Colorado school districts about how they first responded to AI. Some wrote informal guidelines, some banned student use, and some updated their acceptable use policies (McGuire et al., 2026).

sections.body: This part of the book turns to the work of running a school and a district, and it covers four areas of that work. The first is teacher planning and grading, where AI is used in the daily tasks of preparing lessons and giving feedback. The second is assessment and data, including an early warning system that uses data to spot students who may need help. The third is operations, facilities, transportation, and finance, the behind the scenes work that keeps a school running. The fourth is people, leadership, and culture, which is about the adults in the building and how they work together.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The book says these chapters speak most directly to principals, district leaders, and board members, so it treats this as leadership work rather than classroom work. It does not claim that AI fixes everything in these areas, and it holds to the rule that the evidence should guide what a school adopts. The final chapter states the core argument of the Volume in full and sets out a plan for the first 90 days, which suggests the book wants leaders to start small and deliberate. A short conclusion then looks back at what the evidence shows and ahead to what may change, so the book is honest that some things are still unsettled.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The four pages under this section follow the same order as the chapters, so a reader can move through them in sequence. A teacher would go to Teacher Planning, Grading, and Feedback for the classroom facing tasks of planning and marking, while a leader worried about students falling behind would go to Assessment, Data, and the Early Warning System. Someone dealing with budgets, buildings, buses, or money would go to Operations, Facilities, Transportation, and Finance, and anyone thinking about staff, leadership, or the culture of the school would go to People, Leadership, and Culture. Together these pages lead toward the final chapter, which states the core argument and the first 90 days, so a principal or board member can read the four pages and then turn to the plan.
